The 2026 open water fishing season is over for most of us living in the Midwest. With that in mind, I’m in a reflective mood and am looking back at the season. Here are some of those reflections.
p

First, clearing waters mostly because of zebra mussel infiltrations have “changed the game” on lots of lakes I fish. First, clear water means more sunlight penetration resulting in weeds growing deeper than before. Second, many lakes used to have prominent outside weed edges. Those edges are commonly referred to as the “deep weedline.” Now, however, not only do the weeds grow deeper, but those edges are less prominent with “clumps” of weeds appearing at varying depths.
p

The result for me has been finding fish in deeper waters than in the past and trying to figure out ways to fish in and around random weeds. Suffice to say, I don’t have all the answers to this new challenge. But, every day on the water is a learning experience and I’m committed to getting better at catching fish in changing environments.
p

Learning to fish changing lake environments is a challenge. One way, however, to combat changing fish locations is to use today’s cutting edge sonar technologies to find fish. Live sonar like ActiveTarget 2 XL allows anglers to see fish in real time away from the boat and then present lures to those fish. In fact, I used this technology with good success to catch fish in and around deeper weeds this year.
p

While using live sonar did help me catch more fish this year, I still caught lots of fish relying on traditional 2D sonar as well. Some of my best walleye catches this summer came, in fact, using “old school” techniques. I would cruise over suspected walleye holding structure looking for fish on my sonar. Once found, I then pulled live bait rigs through the fish marked on 2D sonar. This is the same method I used successfully at the beginning of my fishing career!
p

In addition to walleyes, I had some dynamite days during the summer’s heat catching big largemouth bass by “dropping” heavy Hack Attack Jigs tipped with Rage Craw trailers to heavy coontail weed clumps. I identified those weeds using 2D sonar and polarized sunglasses.
p
While lakes that are changing and evolving fish methods can present challenges, I can also say that the fishing continues to be very good in many waters I fish!
p
I caught some fish, spent quality time outside with friends and family, and learned a great deal. 2026 was a good fishing season for this angler and here’s to hoping it was for you too!
p
As always, enjoy your time on the water and remember to include a youngster in your next outdoors adventure!
p
Mike Frisch hosts the popular Fishing the Midwest TV series. See www.fishingthemidwest.com.
